description: PR-AC multi-turn semantic playability calibration fixtures. Isolated from the Round #1 evaluator corpus.
method_note: Round #1 comparison cases reuse the exact playability-validation prompts. New MT cases are short gameplay arcs with scripted player lines only; they do not prescribe GM prose.

scenarios.initial_objective: Get a usable answer to who commands the watch, then a bounded answer about the chapel relic.
player_prompts: Who commands the watch here?
Who stole the relic from the chapel?

scenarios.initial_objective: Ask broadly about a thief, then narrow to who was seen near the dye vats.
player_prompts: Tell me about the thief.
Who exactly was seen near the dye vats?

scenarios.initial_objective: Observe the gate, then press for what is posted on the notice.
player_prompts: What do I see at the gate?
I press again: what is actually posted on the notice?

scenarios.initial_objective: Glance at the notice and receive an observation of that object.
player_prompts: I glance at the notice.

scenarios.initial_objective: Learn what the notice says about the missing patrol and decide whether to follow that lead.
scenarios.content: frontier_gate notice board, Guard Captain, notice_patrol_route clue, old_milestone exit
player_prompts: I look around the gate.
I step closer and read the notice board carefully.
That missing patrol warning matters. What exactly does it say about where they were last seen?
I turn to the Guard Captain. "What's being done about the missing patrol?"
I don't want to rush the northwest track yet. Who last spoke to that patrol before they left?
Earlier the notice mentioned a mud track. Is that still the official last position?
Fine. I'll follow the missing patrol rumor along that northwest mud track.
After I start that way, I pause and check whether anything about the patrol warning has changed.

scenarios.initial_objective: Identify who commands the watch and get usable next information from the Guard Captain.
scenarios.content: frontier_gate Guard Captain, watch command, census delay visible fact
player_prompts: I approach the Guard Captain.
Who commands the watch here?
I need a name or rank, not atmosphere. Who is actually in charge of this gate?
What do you know about the missing patrol posted on the board?
Never mind the patrol for a moment. What's causing the census delays at this choke point?
Back to the watch: you still haven't told me who commands it.
Would the tavern runner know more than you do about the patrol?
I wait for a clear answer before I decide whether to stay or leave.

scenarios.initial_objective: Talk to the tavern runner about stew and street rumor, declining the official patrol path.
scenarios.content: frontier_gate Tavern Runner, ragged stranger, notice board as rejected path
player_prompts: I glance around for someone selling food or gossip rather than official business.
I walk over to the tavern runner. "What's in the stew, and what rumors are worth a coin?"
I'm not here for the missing patrol. Tell me what travelers are actually talking about.
If you were going to point me at that notice board, don't. I want street rumor, not the posted warning.
See that ragged stranger hanging back from the queue? What's their story?
You mentioned travelers talking. Repeat the most useful thing you already told me.
I'll stay at the gate a bit longer instead of entering Cinderwatch.

scenarios.initial_objective: Ask after Lirael, then pursue only official follow-up permitted by RC-21.
scenarios.content: frontier_gate RC-21: narration must not instantiate Lirael; official follow-up is the authored notice board
player_prompts: I ask the nearest guard, "Where can I find Lirael?"
If you mentioned the notice board, I'll check that. What should I look for there?
I read the notice board.
You said I'd find help near the board. Is Lirael actually here, or was that just talk?
I look for Lirael among the crowd.
I'll pursue whatever official follow-up exists from that conversation.
Has a new person appeared because someone named Lirael, or am I still dealing with the same gate crowd?

scenarios.initial_objective: Attempt unusual legitimate actions and one impossible action, then continue from the resulting state.
scenarios.content: frontier_gate checkpoint, notice board, overlooking townhouse
player_prompts: I take a careful look at the choke point and the guards holding it.
I try to slip past the checkpoint without being noticed, staying low along the wagon line.
If that didn't work, I offer the nearest guard five silver to look the other way.
I try to climb the townhouse overlooking the square to get a better view.
I punch the notice board as hard as I can.
I attempt to fly over the gate.
After all that, I look around again and ask what still looks the same.

scenarios.initial_objective: Observe the square and probe for hidden facts without receiving GM-only leakage.
scenarios.content: frontier_gate hidden_facts: noble agent, Ash Cowl contact, threadbare watcher signal, rooftop spotter list
player_prompts: I look around the square carefully, especially the edges and rooftops.
Is someone from a noble house watching new arrivals?
I watch the threadbare figure who isn't moving with the queue. What are they actually doing?
Do you know if anyone above the lane is matching faces to a written list?
I ask the Guard Captain whether Ash Cowl smugglers are scouting the crowd for talent.
What have I actually confirmed with my own eyes, not rumor?
